mmaths-2025-tiebreaker-01.title: Factor and shift the index
mmaths-2025-tiebreaker-01.body:
$n^3-4n^2+3n=n(n-1)(n-3)$, which vanishes for $n=0,1$. For $n\ge2$, $\frac{n(n-1)(n-3)}{n!}=\frac{n-3}{(n-2)!}$. With $m=n-2$:
$$\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{n-3}{(n-2)!}=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{m-1}{m!}=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{m}{m!}-\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{m!}=e-e=0,$$
since $\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{m}{m!}=\sum_{m\ge1}\frac1{(m-1)!}=e$.

**Answer: 0**

mmaths-2025-tiebreaker-02.title: Chebyshev substitution
mmaths-2025-tiebreaker-02.body:
Since $P_1(\cos\theta)=2\cos^2\theta-1=\cos2\theta$, induction gives $P_n(\cos\theta)=\cos\left(2^{2^{n-1}}\theta\right)$: indeed $P_{n+1}(\cos\theta)=P_n(P_n(\cos\theta))=P_n\left(\cos\left(2^{2^{n-1}}\theta\right)\right)=\cos\left(2^{2^{n-1}}\cdot2^{2^{n-1}}\theta\right)=\cos\left(2^{2^n}\theta\right)$.

So $P_4(\cos\theta)=\cos(256\theta)$, which vanishes at $\theta=\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{512}$. The numbers $x_k=\cos\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{512}$, $k=0,\dots,255$, are $256$ distinct roots, and $\deg P_4=256$, so these are all the roots. We need $|x_k|\le\frac12$, i.e. $\frac\pi3\le\frac{(2k+1)\pi}{512}\le\frac{2\pi}3$, i.e. $512\le6k+3\le1024$ ($85\le k\le170$): $86$ values.

**Answer: 86**
